title_en: Monster Hunter Outlanders Confirms October 29 Release, with Mobile and PC Versions Launching Together
body_en_md:
Monster Hunter Outlanders is scheduled for release on October 29, 2026. It is the series' first new title designed primarily for mobile devices and will also come to PC. Ahead of launch, Capcom has made several public statements about the game's controls, new monsters, and relationship to existing entries. Meanwhile, developers have continued discussing Monster Hunter Wilds, released in 2025, and its Ascendance expansion at fall 2026 gaming events. Together, the two developments show the franchise advancing on console and mobile platforms in parallel.

## Release Date and Platform Plans

The release date for Monster Hunter Outlanders is confirmed as October 29, 2026. Media reports and official information indicate that the game will be available on mobile devices and PC. The mobile version will offer two control schemes intended to accommodate different player preferences. This expands a franchise that has long relied on consoles and PC to a larger mobile audience. October 29 is the confirmed date for players planning to start on launch day. No information indicates a staggered, platform-specific launch, so current disclosures point to mobile and PC availability on the same day.

## Mobile Control Design

A focus of the mobile version is its two control styles. The options are intended to give players more choice in how they handle hunting gameplay on mobile devices, allowing them to select the approach that best matches their preferences for precision and control. The series' traditional gameplay is built around a structured quest system: players accept quests and complete objectives by hunting or capturing large monsters and collecting resources such as herbs, mushrooms, and monster eggs. Each quest has a 50-minute time limit and receives a performance rating, with rewards including in-game currency and materials. This core structure remains a reference point for understanding the game's design. The two mobile control schemes are intended to make combat rhythms traditionally built around console or PC inputs workable with touchscreens or other mobile controls. Console players will need to judge whether the options suit their established habits, while mobile-first players can test which scheme works best after release.

## New Monsters and Expansion of Series Content

Alongside confirmation of the release date, gameplay footage featuring new monsters has been shown publicly. One newly mentioned ultimate monster is Ruger Aidal, whose boss-fight gameplay and early impressions have appeared in some media coverage. These are pre-release previews intended to show the direction of the game's new monster challenges. The Monster Hunter series has always centered on confronting large monsters with different behavior patterns. Players observe changes in a monster's condition to identify weaknesses and then decide whether to kill, capture, or gather from it. The new-monster footage for Outlanders follows the same basic logic. Ruger Aidal is one of the currently disclosed features closely associated with the launch. Available public information is not sufficient to list all other monster species, the full boss-fight design, or later update content.

## Further Details on Wilds and Ascendance

In parallel with Outlanders, the development team provided additional information about Monster Hunter Wilds and its Ascendance expansion at fall 2026 gaming events. Developers said they would revisit lessons learned from Wilds and make the expansion's Boost Bracers compatible with all 14 weapon types, while also evolving some returning monsters. On difficulty, the expansion's director said players had performed better than expected, so Capcom was recalibrating the difficulty standards for later expansion content. These comments show that Wilds, released in 2025, was still being adjusted in response to player feedback. Wilds was the first game in the franchise to launch simultaneously on all platforms worldwide and became Capcom's fastest-selling game within three days of release. The series had sold 21 million copies by July 5, 2022, exceeded 100 million total sales by May 2024, and surpassed 131 million by July 2026. Wilds continued to drive franchise sales after Monster Hunter: World, Monster Hunter Rise, and their expansions. For players following Ascendance, the current points of interest are the revised difficulty standards and Boost Bracer compatibility across all weapon types.

## Significance for Players and the Industry

For players, Outlanders' release means the series is expanding again to mobile and PC, with two mobile control options. Players will need to consider their platform and control preferences when deciding whether to start on October 29. Those already playing Wilds can also follow Ascendance's difficulty adjustments and changes to weapon compatibility. At the industry level, a new mobile entry alongside continued post-launch adjustments to Wilds shows the franchise retaining its core hunting loop while adapting controls and difficulty to different platforms and player feedback. Current public information does not include pricing, specific storefront arrangements, or a post-launch update schedule, so those details cannot yet be treated as confirmed.

## Details Still to Be Confirmed

Before the October 29 release, players will want to learn about the actual control experience, the differences between the two control schemes, and Ruger Aidal's full in-game profile. Further information about Wilds: Ascendance is expected to focus on difficulty recalibration, weapon compatibility, and changes to returning monsters. Public disclosures have provided the release date, platforms, mobile controls, new-monster footage, and some development details about the Wilds expansion. Pricing, storefront arrangements, and the post-launch update plan still require official information. Players hoping to start on launch day should confirm that their platform meets the game's requirements and consider which mobile control option best suits them.

title_en: Accounting for U.S. Military Operations Against Iran Lags as Household Costs Rise, Fueling Debate Over Fiscal Priorities
body_en_md:
As of September 27, 2026, the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) had published no estimate of the cost of Operation Epic Fury, the U.S. military campaign against Iran that began on February 28, 2026. Meanwhile, transportation, food, energy, electronics, housing, and other household costs in the United States had continued to rise during 2026. The lack of transparency around the campaign's expenses, combined with pressure on everyday budgets, had prompted broad debate over public-spending priorities.

## War-Cost Accounting Runs Into an Information Barrier

In March 2026, Rep. Brendan Boyle, the ranking member of the House Budget Committee, asked the CBO to prepare a nonpartisan cost estimate for Operation Epic Fury. The CBO began the work and was initially expected to release preliminary findings in summer 2026. But by September it had published no related public data. Reports said the agency had encountered obstacles in obtaining information: the Pentagon had not provided a complete breakdown of the operation's expenses, delaying the estimate. The specific fiscal cost of the campaign launched in late February therefore remained opaque.

## Household Costs Across the United States Rise in 2026

A broad range of household costs increased in 2026, covering food, energy, electronics, housing, pet care, and entertainment. Official data identified transportation costs as a major factor pushing up prices for end products. Media reports said the cost of moving goods across regions continued to rise for nearly all products in 2026. This affected physical-goods distribution and raised prices for delivery and logistics services, with effects on retail prices for cars, food, electronics, and other categories.

In food, reports said prices for steak, tomatoes, and delivered meals remained high in New York, while the cost of buying food for Thanksgiving dinner in 2026 was notably higher than in previous years. In energy, a fuel-price increase calculator showed that rising gasoline prices since the start of Operation Epic Fury had added substantial costs for U.S. households. Polling also indicated that consumers were broadly pessimistic about gasoline prices over the following six months.

In electronics, reports compared the launch price of the original Xbox in 2001 with prices for comparable products in 2026, finding an increase well above inflation and pointing to rising component costs. Building a PC in 2026 with performance comparable to a PlayStation 5 Pro, as well as buying Apple's M5 Ultra Mac Studio, cost substantially more than the previous generation. The main reason cited was sharp year-over-year increases in memory and storage prices: memory was about four times as expensive as in 2025, while storage was about twice as expensive. Memory and storage accounted for more than 20% of the bill of materials for consumer electronics in 2026, up from 10% to 18% before the increases. For Apple's top-end M5 Ultra model, hardware costs had risen by $2,400 to $2,600 compared with the previous generation, while the retail price had increased by nearly 60%. Prices for new 2026 products from motorcycle-helmet brand Cardo had also risen noticeably.

In housing, a national cost index updated in March 2026 put the median cost of a midrange remodel of a 50-square-foot guest bathroom at $11,625. The median cost of replacing the roof on a 2,000-square-foot detached home was $18,214.

In pet care, the American Pet Products Association reported that U.S. pet-industry spending totaled $157 billion in 2025. Bureau of Labor Statistics data released in March 2026 showed that, in February 2026, prices for pet food and treats were up 1.4% year over year, pet supplies and accessories were up 1.8%, and veterinary services were up 5.3%. Annual pet ownership costs ranged from at least $1,390 to more than $5,200.

In entertainment and sports, reports said rising living costs were a major reason more people were reducing social activities and spending more time alone. High social and entertainment expenses had forced some people to change their lifestyles and go out less often. Other reports described higher entertainment spending among New York residents in fall 2026, as well as increases in the price of beer at Vancouver Canucks home games, the cost of attending an entire Carolina Hurricanes season, and the buyout payment for the University of South Carolina football coach. Manchester City's financial-fair-play ruling in European soccer also prompted discussion about the financial costs that the club's years of success had imposed on other clubs.

## Debate Over the Allocation of Public Spending

Against the backdrop of rising household costs, the allocation of public spending attracted greater attention. The cost of Operation Epic Fury remained unpublished, and reports said a new round of taxpayer-funded advertising by the Trump administration also lacked transparency, leaving the public unable to assess whether the spending was justified. Research from Columbia Business School suggested that eliminating extreme poverty worldwide would cost far less than the public expected. The costs of healthcare plans proposed by California gubernatorial candidates Becerra and Hilton, as well as data-center upgrades in Oregon, were subject to close scrutiny. These contrasts fueled questions about public fiscal priorities. Official data also showed that the savings needed for North Carolina residents to retire comfortably had risen substantially, adding to retirement pressure on younger and middle-aged adults.

## Guidance for Different Groups

Ordinary consumers, especially residents of high-cost cities such as New York, face rising expenses for food, delivery, entertainment, and energy. They can follow the monthly Consumer Price Index (CPI) data released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, plan household budgets carefully, and avoid unnecessary impulse purchases. Consumers planning to buy technology products or renovate their homes can watch for promotional periods and consider waiting for component or building-material prices to ease rather than making nonessential purchases at elevated prices. Pet-owning households may buy shelf-stable food in bulk and consider pet insurance to offset rising veterinary costs. People concerned about public finances can follow the CBO's eventual estimate for Operation Epic Fury and relevant House Budget Committee hearings, and use public channels to express concerns about spending transparency.

As of publication, the CBO had not announced a timetable for its final cost estimate of Operation Epic Fury. Inflationary pressure in the United States remained ongoing, and the allocation of public spending was expected to be a focus of congressional debate.

title_en: New York Prosecutors Reopen Criminal Investigation Into 2024 Cornell University Fraternity Gang-Rape Allegations
body_en_md:
In late September 2026, Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten announced that prosecutors were reopening a criminal investigation into allegations of a group sexual assault at Cornell University's Chi Phi fraternity in 2024. The decision followed a September 16 civil lawsuit filed by the plaintiff, identified as “Jane Doe,” in New York State Supreme Court, renewing public questions about why prosecutors had not brought criminal charges at the time. Van Houten assigned an experienced senior prosecutor with a background in sexual-assault cases to handle the preliminary review. Once prosecutors determine the direction of any potential charges, they plan to present the evidence to a Tompkins County grand jury to consider whether an indictment is warranted.

## Core Allegations and Timeline

According to the plaintiff's 101-page civil complaint and media reports, Jane Doe was a 20-year-old Cornell student at the time of the alleged incident. In October 2024, at the Chi Phi fraternity house on Cornell's Ithaca campus, seven fraternity members allegedly forced her to take ketamine, smoke marijuana, and drink alcohol. The complaint says she became completely incapacitated and was sexually assaulted for more than four hours. On November 8, 2024, Jane Doe reported the incident to Cornell University Police. However, according to police-statement records made public by prosecutors, she said at the time that the drug use and sexual activity had been voluntary, that she had been conscious, and that the encounters were consensual. That account is fundamentally at odds with the allegations in the current civil lawsuit. On September 16, 2026, Jane Doe filed a civil complaint in New York State Supreme Court naming the seven students and Cornell University as defendants. Claims include negligence, breach of contract, sexual assault and battery, and violations of New York's Human Rights Law. She also alleges that the university protected the students, obstructed them from testifying to law enforcement, and suppressed her voice during its handling of the matter. The complaint further alleges that Cornell gave the seven students an opportunity to mitigate disciplinary consequences by submitting papers, a characterization the university disputes.

## Prosecutors' Stated Basis for Reopening the Investigation

In a nine-page statement released in September, Van Houten explained that his office's November 2024 decision not to bring criminal charges had been based primarily on Jane Doe's statement to police at the time. The allegations in the September 2026 civil lawsuit, he said, were “diametrically different” from that earlier account. Prosecutors could not have based their 2024 charging decision on a complaint filed two years later. He said the purpose of reopening the investigation was to determine whether additional evidence existed in November 2024 that prosecutors had not then possessed and that could have changed their assessment enough for a grand jury to find that a crime had occurred. Reports said the renewed investigation also followed other related allegations that had recently emerged, although details had not been made public. Van Houten assigned a senior prosecutor experienced in sexual-assault cases to begin reviewing the evidence. The case is expected to be presented to a grand jury after prosecutors complete their assessment of possible charges.

## Cornell's Response and Its Earlier Disciplinary Process

After prosecutors announced the reopened investigation, Cornell issued a statement saying it supported the decision. The university also defended its earlier handling of the matter, saying it had conducted a thorough Title IX investigation over several months. It later convened a panel of trained faculty and staff members, heard testimony from both sides over multiple days, and ultimately imposed expulsions and suspensions on the students involved. The university did not disclose the specific disciplinary actions taken against each student. Jane Doe's complaint, however, says Cornell did not impose sufficiently serious penalties on the alleged perpetrators and instead protected the students, prevented them from testifying to law enforcement, and suppressed her voice. It characterizes the university's conduct as “beyond the bounds of what the community should tolerate” and as showing disregard for the consequences. Jeremy Saland, an attorney for the students, previously told CNN that prosecutors declined to bring charges in 2024 because Jane Doe's allegations “simply did not exist” at the time, and that her statement clearly showed the conduct had been voluntary.

## Current Status and Possible Next Steps

The case remains in the early stages of the reopened criminal investigation. No criminal charges have been filed, and no date has been announced for grand-jury consideration. Those directly affected include Jane Doe, who is pursuing civil claims against Cornell and the students and may also need to cooperate with the criminal investigation; the seven accused students, who have faced university expulsions or suspensions and could face criminal penalties if charges are brought and convictions obtained; Cornell students, particularly fraternity members, for whom the case may prompt further discussion about fraternity culture and campus sexual-assault prevention; and the Tompkins County justice system, which must devote resources to reviewing a complex case spanning two years.

The public will be watching three developments. First, prosecutors must complete their evidence review, determine whether specific criminal charges are appropriate, and decide when to present the matter to a grand jury. Second, the grand jury will consider the evidence; if it finds sufficient grounds for an indictment, prosecutors may formally bring criminal charges. Third, Jane Doe's civil lawsuit will proceed under New York civil procedure, including discovery and pretrial motions. Cornell may face further questions about its earlier process, and additional related allegations could emerge.

title_en: Reviews of Two Works Titled Silent Show a Sharp Divide: Platform Performance Varies and the Series Draws Mixed Reactions
body_en_md:
Recent reviews from 49 media outlets and users show sharply divided responses to two works sharing the title Silent. Townfall, a 2024 spin-off in the Silent Hill franchise, performs as expected on PS5 and PS5 Pro but has serious optimization problems on PC. The Japanese romance series Silent, which aired in 2022, has also prompted renewed discussion, with strongly divided reactions.

## The Game Performs Well on Consoles but Is Poorly Optimized on PC

Developed jointly by Konami and Annapurna Interactive, Silent Hill: Townfall is the latest spin-off in the franchise. It moves the setting from the series' familiar American town to the coast of Scotland and explores shame and psychological trauma, taking on psychological-horror themes that the franchise has addressed less often. Since release, it has attracted attention from franchise fans and horror-game players.

Many reviews praised its atmosphere, psychological horror, and environmental art. The bleak Scottish coastal setting, oppressive ambient sound, and detailed portrayal of the protagonist's inner trauma continue the series' recognizable style. One review said its “merciless darkness and unsettling horror” met franchise fans' expectations, making it appealing to players who enjoy psychological horror.

On consoles, the PS5 and PS5 Pro versions received consistently positive assessments. Reviews said frame rates were stable, visuals met expectations, loading was fast, and stuttering was rare. The game made good use of the PS5 Pro's performance enhancements, providing a smooth experience in line with expectations for a current-generation horror title.

On PC, however, optimization was the biggest complaint. A third-party hardware outlet tested 35 mainstream graphics cards. Even a midrange-to-high-end card at the RTX 4070 level reportedly struggled to maintain a stable 60 frames per second at maximum settings in 1440p. At 4K, frame-rate fluctuations exceeded 30%. Some scenes had missing textures or failed model loading, and crashes occurred in more than 15% of tests. Keyboard-and-mouse support also had problems, including incorrect key mappings and an inability to adjust sensitivity. Steam Deck reviews said the game reached only 30 frames per second in handheld mode, with heavily compressed visuals and interface text that was nearly impossible to read.

Beyond PC optimization, stealth and combat systems were also major points of criticism. Reviews described the stealth mechanics as rigid, enemy AI as inconsistent, and combat feedback as weak, creating a sharp contrast with the otherwise strong atmosphere. Players said stealth detection was imprecise and often led to pointless deaths, hurting the overall experience. Mainstream review scores were concentrated around three to four stars out of five. Some outlets described the game as having “excellent atmosphere but weak gameplay,” while others said it maintained tension but ultimately felt somewhat flat and failed to leave a lasting impression.

## The Television Series Wins Praise for Emotion but Draws Criticism for Its Ending

The other work attracting attention is the Japanese romance series Silent, which aired in 2022 and stars Haruna Kawaguchi and Ren Meguro. It tells the story of two people who fell in love in high school, separated after the male lead unexpectedly lost his hearing and withdrew without explanation, and reunited eight years later to resolve their misunderstandings. The series depicts the daily experiences and psychological state of people who become deaf with considerable detail, including sign-language use and the social difficulties faced by people with hearing impairments. Recent rounds of discussion have produced sharply divided reactions.

Positive reviews generally praised its tight pacing, noting that its 11 episodes contained little unnecessary material. Viewers found the leads' chemistry natural and the emotional storytelling restrained rather than melodramatic. Many felt it addressed hearing disability more deeply than comparable works and had a strong emotional impact. Scores were often between 8.5 and 8.7 out of 10. Some viewers called it a rare romance that could be emotionally understood without special background knowledge and said its emotional portrayal even surpassed that of the similarly themed classic First Love.

Negative reactions focused on what viewers saw as a breakdown in the later story. Some said the writers lost control of the central themes after the midpoint. The earlier emphasis on trauma, self-acceptance, and understanding faded, while the ending shifted toward a romantic storyline that had not been sufficiently developed. Critics said the logic became inconsistent and characters acted against their earlier characterization, making the experience feel disjointed. Some low-scoring viewers said the series had the potential to become a classic but wasted a strong premise, describing it as mediocre or disappointing.

## Different Audiences Should Make Their Own Choices

The two works affect different audiences. For Silent Hill: Townfall, the core audience is horror-game players and franchise fans. PS5 and PS5 Pro owners can expect an experience that meets current-generation horror-game standards. PC players, especially those hoping to play at 4K with a midrange or high-end graphics card, should be cautious and consider waiting for an official optimization patch before buying. Steam Deck users are advised not to prioritize the game.

For the Japanese series Silent, the main audience consists of Japanese-drama viewers and people interested in hearing-disability themes. Viewers who enjoy slower emotional dramas or are interested in hearing-related issues may find value in its character work and subject matter. Those who prefer tightly logical, fast-paced storytelling may find the plot slow and the ending unsatisfying, and may want to adjust their expectations.

Konami and Annapurna Interactive have not announced a specific release date for a PC optimization patch for Townfall. PC players can follow the developers' official social accounts or wait for hardware communities to complete compatibility tests across graphics cards before deciding whether to buy. Console players can play the current version without waiting.

The Japanese series currently has ratings around 8 out of 10 on major review sites. Viewers can decide whether to watch based on their interest in romance and hearing-disability themes rather than feeling compelled to join the discussion.

title_en: Treasury Yields Approach a 20-Year High, Putting Pressure on Stocks and Real Estate
body_en_md:
U.S. Treasury yields continued to rise. The 10-year yield had reached its highest level since 2007, while the 30-year yield approached a 20-year high. As yields neared or crossed the psychologically important 5% threshold, stocks came under pressure, gold and cryptocurrencies retreated, and commercial real estate faced refinancing strain. The federal government's net interest costs had also exceeded spending on Medicare and the military. Markets broadly expected the Federal Reserve to raise rates again at its October meeting, pushing up the Treasury Department's borrowing costs. The next major focus was the upcoming employment report and whether Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent would intervene to bring down long-term rates.

## Yields Reach Multi-Year Highs as Oil Prices Rise

Media reports said the 10-year Treasury yield had briefly reached 5.165% in recent trading, its highest level since July 2007, before settling near 5.163%. Other data put its closing yield at 5.11%, up sharply from 4.96% in the previous session. The 30-year yield rose to a range of 5.40% to 5.46%, its highest level since June 2004. Meanwhile, oil prices recovered to more than $103 a barrel. Several reports said the relationship between oil prices and Treasury yields had become the tightest since 1990.

Markets were highly sensitive to Treasury-yield movements. Several institutions said 5% carried significant psychological weight, making the movement of long-term yields around that threshold a central concern for investors. In a recent seven-year Treasury auction, the Treasury Department sold $44 billion at a yield of 5.085%, the highest since April 1993. In a long-term bond buyback operation, the department purchased only $4.1 billion, below its previously established $6 billion limit, indicating investor caution toward long-term borrowing. A five-year Treasury auction had also recorded its highest yield since 2006 amid weak demand, helping push the 10-year yield's one-day increase to its largest in four months.

## Pressure on the Federal Budget and Borrowing Costs

The Congressional Budget Office's monthly budget review showed that the federal government's net interest costs reached $1.05 trillion in the first 11 months of fiscal 2026, up 12% from the same period a year earlier. That amount exceeded Medicare spending of $976 billion and Defense Department military spending of $833 billion over the same period. The federal government was spending more on debt service than on either Medicare or the military. Rising borrowing costs were materially changing the structure of the federal budget.

Treasury Department data confirmed the trend: as yields reached successive multi-year highs, the government's borrowing costs rose. Several media outlets mentioned the possibility that Treasury Secretary Bessent might use certain measures to bring the 10-year yield down, but no specific approach had been established. Market participants said the key questions were whether long-term yields could remain around 5% and whether financial markets and the real economy could coexist with higher rates.

## Links Among Stocks, Gold, Crypto Assets, and the Dollar

Rising Treasury yields put clear pressure on stocks. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell more than 300 points early in the week, and technology shares also declined. Several outlets attributed the market drop mainly to the combined pressure of higher Treasury yields and rising oil prices. Institutional analysts said the relationship between Treasury yields and stock earnings yields was approaching a turning point: as the cost of capital rises, equities become less attractive relative to risk-free rates. JPMorgan said the stock market's potential “break point” could fall between 5.5% and 6%, given that spending on artificial intelligence, healthcare, and services was less sensitive to interest rates. Invesco analysts had begun reducing exposure to stocks and emerging-market bond funds, the latter of which had experienced their largest outflows in months.

Gold was also pressured by the surge in Treasury yields and expectations of another Federal Reserve rate increase, falling more than 3.5% in a single day. Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, and Dogecoin all declined as Treasury yields rose. Although analysts had described Bitcoin's decline as a possible buying opportunity, overall market sentiment remained under pressure. The dollar stayed strong amid expectations of another Fed rate increase, and its strength further intensified capital outflows from emerging-market bonds.

## Direct Effects on Commercial Real Estate and the Broader Economy

The impact of higher Treasury yields was especially direct for commercial real estate. With the 10-year yield near multi-year highs, the sector was facing refinancing pressure. Higher long-term rates mean property owners must pay more to refinance maturing debt, while investors have become less willing to commit to long-term borrowing amid inflation and fiscal uncertainty. For commercial-property investors and homeowners, the high-rate environment means more difficult refinancing, higher holding costs, and potential cash-flow pressure for some projects.

For ordinary consumers, rising Treasury yields typically feed through to mortgage rates and other consumer-credit costs, making home purchases and borrowing more expensive. For employers and businesses, higher capital costs may restrain expansion, particularly in interest-rate-sensitive industries. For investors, rising yields are repricing the risk-return relationship across global assets, as higher risk-free rates compress the premium available on risk assets.

## Market Expectations and What to Watch Next

The central market question was why Treasury yields could continue approaching and setting multi-year highs. Several reports said strong economic data supported expectations that the Federal Reserve would raise rates at its October meeting, while renewed inflation concerns pushed yields higher. Treasury auction results indicated weakening demand for long-term bonds, forcing up government borrowing costs. Bessent might need to take some form of action to lower the 10-year yield, but no policy details had been made clear.

The upcoming employment report was the next major focus. Some analysts said the report could push both the 10-year and 30-year yields higher: if employment remained strong, expectations of another Fed rate increase would be reinforced. Investors were also watching for a meaningful turning point in the relationship between Treasury yields and stock earnings yields, and whether financial markets could remain stable in a higher-rate environment. Commercial real-estate professionals and homeowners needed to monitor refinancing windows and rate-lock timing. For stock and bond investors, yields in the 5% to 6% range could become an important reference point for measuring pressure on risk assets.

title_en: Trump and Johnson to Convene AI Executives at the White House on September 29, Focusing on Safety and Competition With China
body_en_md:
At 12:30 p.m. local time on September 29, President Donald Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson were scheduled to host a closed-door AI policy meeting in the White House East Room. Executives from several leading AI companies had confirmed their attendance. The central issue was how to balance technological innovation, safety controls, and national strategic interests as U.S. competition with China intensified and debate over AI safety risks grew. The White House had not announced what specific policies might follow the meeting.

## Background and Central Tensions

The global artificial-intelligence race was accelerating, while disagreements within the United States over how to regulate the technology continued to widen. Leading AI companies including Anthropic and OpenAI had issued public warnings that rapidly advancing advanced AI systems could pose catastrophic risks to human survival. They called on governments to lead coordinated oversight and slow the development of powerful AI. On the other side, the Trump administration and senior congressional Republicans generally viewed maintaining a competitive advantage over China in AI as a core strategic interest. They worried that strict regulation would slow U.S. companies' development and allow China to take the lead.

The day before the White House meeting, on the evening of September 28, Trump had held his first one-on-one meeting with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei at Joint Base Andrews. It was viewed as a warm-up for the broader discussion the next day. Trump had also publicly proposed creating a federal “AI force” to coordinate domestic AI research resources, further highlighting the technology's priority in U.S. strategy.

## Participants and Official Positions

Media reports said those confirmed for the September 29 meeting included Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, Google CEO Sundar Pichai, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, SpaceX AI CEO Elon Musk, and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. Their companies span major parts of the U.S. AI sector, including computing power, foundation-model development, and technology platforms.

Before the meeting, Johnson told Fox Business that the central goal was clear: “We don't need to pause AI development, and we cannot overregulate it, or we will lose the race against China, which would threaten the interests of every American. Innovation must continue, but we need to find the right balance. That is what this meeting is about.”

Trump had repeatedly played down AI safety concerns, calling them a “hoax.” His central concern, he said, was that if the United States failed to win the AI race, it would be placed in a very unfavorable position. He had also claimed that the United States was far ahead of China in AI and that federal agencies, including the Justice Department, had established relevant technology-control mechanisms. Senate Majority Leader John Thune had made clear that he would not attend the meeting.

## Policy Disagreements and Industry Requests

The meeting came as members of both parties in Congress had recently shown interest in AI legislation. A former Anthropic researcher had publicly warned that the rapid development of powerful AI could create irreversible catastrophic risks, prompting several bipartisan lawmakers to call for urgent congressional regulation. Johnson, however, had ruled out the prospect of Congress passing mandatory AI regulations in the short term. He argued that an emergency session to regulate AI would weaken U.S. companies' competitiveness and ultimately cause the country to lose its strategic contest with China.

The AI industry's requests differed noticeably from the position of senior Republicans. Several leading companies had called for slowing the development of powerful AI and establishing mandatory safety-evaluation systems. They wanted high-risk AI systems to undergo prior review and supported globally consistent rules to prevent harmful loss of control. The central disagreement was that Republican leaders prioritized maintaining the pace of technological development and preserving an advantage over China, while some AI professionals believed that rapid development without adequate safeguards could create systemic risks far greater than the potential benefits.

## Possible Outcomes and Expectations

The meeting was the first time since the Trump administration took office that it had convened senior congressional leaders and technology-company representatives for closed-door consultations specifically on AI. The White House had not announced whether it would issue a concrete regulatory framework or executive order afterward.

Industry observers said strict nationwide mandatory AI regulation was unlikely in the short term because senior Republicans generally opposed it and regarded competition with China as a strategic priority. A more likely direction would be nonbinding guidance encouraging industry self-regulation, combined with increased federal funding for AI research to widen the U.S. technological lead.

The outcome could directly affect three groups: AI workers and companies, whose compliance costs and research priorities would be shaped by policy; civil-society organizations and researchers focused on AI safety, who would watch whether mandatory safeguards were included; and participants in U.S.-China technology competition, who would monitor changes in America's AI strategy. The next developments to watch were the White House's official statement, whether Congress introduced related legislation, and whether AI companies adjusted their safety-development rules in response.

title_en: Ukraine Prepares for a Winter Internet Shutdown as Russia Targets Network Infrastructure
body_en_md:
The Ukrainian government was preparing for a worst-case scenario in which Russia could attack internet infrastructure. The effort had become a central part of Ukraine's winter defense plan. As Russia accumulated large numbers of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and jet-powered Shahed drones, Ukrainian officials warned that Moscow could systematically strike power grids, communications facilities, and internet infrastructure during the winter. The goal, they said, would be to cut off civilian services and weaken public morale. Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said on September 27 that Ukraine was better prepared for this winter than it had been last year, but that the adversary's capabilities had also improved, making the coming confrontation difficult.

## Ukraine's Specific Winter Preparations

In his September 27 remarks, Koretskyi said Ukraine had expanded its power-generation capacity over the previous year and equipped more critical civilian facilities with auxiliary backup power systems. The government said physical protection at key infrastructure nodes had improved, strategic equipment and spare-parts reserves were larger, and emergency repair teams and specialized machinery had been strengthened. Koretskyi also acknowledged that Moscow had improved its aerial tactics and offensive assets, including jet-powered Shahed drones and large stocks of ballistic and cruise missiles accumulated specifically for winter.

According to Ukrainian government figures, nearly one-third of Ukrainian communities could not maintain basic services for a full day without electricity, and 78% lacked sufficient reserves of fuel for generators. To prepare for a prolonged outage, Ukraine was building up large reserves of food and water. The government said regional military administrations, municipal leaders, state-owned companies, and relevant agencies had completed substantial work. Although some preparations were behind schedule, overall readiness had improved materially.

## Russia's Infrastructure Strike Plans

Ukraine accused Russia of preparing a systematic winter campaign against Ukrainian infrastructure. Ukrainian monitoring agencies reported that Russia was assembling 28 hypersonic and ballistic missiles and about 200 Shahed drones at forward positions. Potential targets included energy facilities, metal smelters, chemical facilities, and defense-industry companies across five regions. The Kremenchuk oil refinery in the Poltava region was among the sites identified as a Russian target.

Ukraine warned that Russia's winter strategy was intended to weaken civilians' ability to live normally by cutting electricity and communications, and to pressure the government into making concessions over energy supplies. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov told the United Nations that Russia rejected the idea of a partial ceasefire, a position President Vladimir Putin had also reiterated. Moscow said it would consider ending the conflict only on its own terms.

## Ukraine's Ability to Strike Back

Ukraine was strengthening its ability to retaliate against Russian infrastructure attacks. The Ukrainian Defense Ministry said the country was preparing to conduct deep strikes against enemy territory as one means of weakening Russia's ability to continue the war. Ukrainian officials also emphasized that stronger sanctions pressure on Russia remained necessary.

On August 16, former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov announced that Ukraine would deploy domestically produced ballistic missiles within three to six months to strike deep targets inside Russia. That timetable suggested Ukraine could have the capability before the end of 2026, marking a significant shift in the country's sovereign defense manufacturing. Fedorov said that although he was unsure whether he would return to government service, his focus remained on ending the war and rebuilding the country.

On August 15, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed a Ukrainian strike on a facility belonging to a space agency in Samara, Russia. Ukraine also reported attacks on two Russian oil refineries.

## International Support and Cooperation

France was working to help Ukraine narrow its defense gap. French President Emmanuel Macron and Zelenskyy signed a formal contract for SAMP/T air-defense systems and interceptors. Ukraine committed to using EU loan funds to manufacture the systems domestically. The two countries were also jointly developing an anti-ballistic system called FREYJA. France was betting that Ukraine could maintain its ability to defend itself and sought to strengthen that capacity through technological cooperation.

On September 7, Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevhenii Hmara and Armed Forces Commander-in-Chief Mykhailo Drapatyi met with national security advisers from France, Germany, and the United Kingdom. Ukraine outlined its priorities for air-to-air and missile defense. It was also preparing for the possibility that Russia might announce another wave of mobilization.

## What to Watch Next

The Ukrainian government warned that Russia could attack internet infrastructure during the winter, affecting civilians' communications and access to information. Residents were advised to prepare for prolonged power and communications outages, including by storing food and water and arranging backup power equipment. The government urged people to monitor local air-raid alerts and learn the locations of nearby shelters.

For investors and industry participants, Ukraine's energy and communications infrastructure could face a severe test during the winter, potentially affecting operations in related sectors. International partners were helping Ukraine strengthen its defenses by providing air-defense systems and financial support, but the country continued to face serious challenges.

Ukraine said it would continue strengthening infrastructure protection and preparing for possible further Russian attacks. The government called on the international community to maintain sanctions pressure on Russia and provide necessary defensive support. Ukraine was also preparing to resume peace talks with the United States and Russia, with another round expected in October.

title_en: Fall 2026 Series American Hostage: Release and Streaming Schedule
body_en_md:
The crime thriller American Hostage premiered on the U.S. streaming service MGM+ on September 20, 2026, with its first two episodes released simultaneously. One new episode was then scheduled every Sunday, with the eight-episode first-season finale set for November 1, 2026. Jon Hamm stars as Fred Heckman, a 1970s Indianapolis radio journalist, while Giovanni Ribisi plays hostage-taker Tony Kiritsis. The series is adapted from the 2022 podcast American Hostage, which was itself based on a real hostage crisis in Indianapolis in February 1977. The show's Rotten Tomatoes critics' score was about 90%, but was based on only a little more than a dozen early reviews. For viewers, the key information is where and when to watch, the real event behind the adaptation, and the questions it raises about journalism and true events.

## Streaming Platforms and Schedule

American Hostage is exclusive to MGM+ in the United States. Subscribers who add the MGM+ channel through Prime Video can also watch it there. There was no evidence that the series had launched on other major streaming platforms. New episodes were scheduled for Sundays at 9 p.m. Eastern Time. The first two episodes, “My Town Indy” and “McMahon, Martinis & Madness,” were released on September 20. One episode was to follow each week through the November 1 season finale, “Break the Bank.” Viewers who wanted to catch up before the fourth episode needed an active MGM+ subscription because the series was not available on other major U.S. platforms.

International distribution varied by region. HBO Max carried the series in France, Poland, and parts of Central and Eastern Europe. MGM+ handled the United Kingdom, Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, and Latin America. Movistar Plus+ and Stan were also among the international buyers. The series had its world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival in early September 2026.

## Based on the 1977 Indianapolis Hostage Crisis

The series draws on a real hostage crisis in Indianapolis in February 1977. After his property was foreclosed on, Tony Kiritsis entered a mortgage brokerage office and took mortgage broker Dick Hall hostage. He attached the barrel and trigger of a shotgun to a wire looped around Hall's neck. Kiritsis called it a “dead man's line”: if police shot him, his body weight would pull the wire and cause the gun to fire, killing Hall. Kiritsis then took Hall through the streets of Indianapolis before hiding in his apartment for three days.

During the standoff, Kiritsis repeatedly called local radio station WIBC and demanded a live interview with news anchor Fred Heckman. While performing his journalistic duties, Heckman unexpectedly became one of the central communicators in the crisis. The ordeal lasted about 63 hours. Both the series and the original podcast retell the event across eight episodes. Hamm had also played Heckman in the podcast, which was produced by Criminal Content and initially released through Amazon Music and Wondery. The television adaptation was developed by Shawn Ryan and Eileen Myers and produced for MGM+.

## Cast and Character Relationships

Jon Hamm plays Fred Heckman, a veteran journalist with 22 years of radio experience in Indianapolis who is known locally as “the most trusted voice in the news.” In the series, Heckman has gradually moved away from the reporting that originally advanced his career. He is considering a lucrative offer from CBS Radio's New York headquarters and preparing to leave Indianapolis.

Giovanni Ribisi plays Tony Kiritsis, a former car salesman driven to an extreme act by a mortgage dispute. Kiritsis accuses Dick Hall and his family of approving a loan despite knowing he could not repay it, intending to take the 17 acres Kiritsis hoped to develop into a shopping destination anchored by a steakhouse. Kiritsis is willing to speak only with Heckman, hoping to obtain an apology, immunity, and a path back to the “American Dream.”

Kristoffer Polaha plays hostage Dick Hall. William Jackson Harper plays Heckman's colleague Ben Hairston, and Mireille Enos plays Heckman's wife, Barbara. The series portrays Heckman and Barbara as having a stable marriage and three children, although the children are not relevant to the plot.

## Central Story and Questions of Journalistic Ethics

The story focuses not only on the hostage crisis but also on how Heckman's role changes during it. Kiritsis insists on speaking live with the “most trusted voice in the news,” forcing Heckman back into frontline reporting. The series suggests that the experience rekindles Heckman's interest in journalism while testing his ethical boundaries and worrying his colleague Ben Hairston. Local police, meanwhile, are dealing with rumors of misconduct within the department and trying to find a peaceful resolution.

For viewers, the series depicts the complicated position of a journalist who is both a reporter and a participant in the central communication channel during a breaking crisis. It also explores the blurred boundary between live news coverage and crisis negotiation.

## Early Reviews and Viewer Considerations

As of September 20, American Hostage had a Rotten Tomatoes Tomatometer score of about 90%, based on only a little more than a dozen reviews, so the sample was still small. Some critics compared the series with True Detective and Mad Men, praising its faithful adaptation of the podcast and its tense dramatization of a real event. Others said that although Hamm's subtle facial performance was compelling, some material could have been completed in fewer episodes.

Viewers should note that distribution differs outside the United States. U.S. viewers who want to catch up before the fourth episode need an MGM+ subscription or the Prime Video add-on. New episodes arrive Sundays at 9 p.m. Eastern Time, and the eight-episode season ends November 1. The series is a fictionalized adaptation: although based on a real event, its dialogue, character details, and pacing are dramatic reconstructions and should not be treated as a complete historical record of the 1977 crisis.

## What to Expect and How to Watch

Anyone planning to watch should first confirm the platform available in their region. In the United States, MGM+ or its Prime Video add-on is the main option. HBO Max carries the show in France, Poland, and parts of Central and Eastern Europe. MGM+ handles the United Kingdom, Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, and parts of Latin America. New episodes arrive Sundays at 9 p.m. Eastern Time, with the season finale on November 1. The first two episodes were released on September 20, followed by weekly installments.

Because the high early score is based on a small number of reviews, the overall assessment may change as more episodes become available. Viewers interested in the distinction between real events and dramatization may first want to learn about the 63-hour February 1977 crisis in which Kiritsis held mortgage broker Dick Hall and demanded a live radio interview. Comparing that history with the series can help distinguish the factual framework from the show's creative additions.

title_en: The Federal Reserve's September Rate Hike: What Makes It Different, Who Is Affected, and What Comes Next
body_en_md:
In September 2026, the Federal Reserve announced a 25-basis-point increase in the federal funds rate, keeping the target range at the high level of 5.25% to 5.5%. It was the latest adjustment in the current monetary-tightening cycle. Financial media said the move differed from previous rate-hike cycles because inflation had not cooled as much as expected, the labor market remained relatively resilient, and high rates were being transmitted more directly to households, businesses, and investors. The high-rate environment was expected to last at least through the first half of 2027.

## Background and What Makes This Cycle Different

The main basis for the rate increase was official employment and inflation data released by the U.S. Department of Labor. The August nonfarm payrolls report showed that the economy added 327,000 jobs, far above the market expectation of 170,000. Average hourly earnings rose 4.2% year over year, still significantly above the Fed's long-term 2% inflation target. The August Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 3.1% year over year, while core CPI, excluding food and energy, increased 3.8%. Both readings were above expectations, indicating that inflation was more persistent than the Fed had previously judged.

Media reports said previous Fed tightening cycles generally began during periods of rapidly rising inflation and shifted relatively quickly to rate cuts after inflation fell noticeably and the labor market showed signs of cooling. High rates usually lasted no more than a year. This time, however, the increase came amid recurring inflation and unresolved mismatches between labor supply and demand. In his latest remarks, the Fed chair said rates would remain elevated for longer and that the central bank would not begin cutting rates in 2026. This meant that the drag of high rates on the real economy could last longer than in previous cycles.

Reports also said the seven-year Treasury yield rose to about 4.2% after the increase, its highest level since 2024. That directly raised the pricing benchmark for longer-term credit, including mortgages and auto loans, and changed valuation dynamics for bonds, stocks, and other assets.

## Direct Effects on Different Groups

The first group is homebuyers and existing homeowners. Reports said the average rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage rose to 6.8% after the Fed's move, the highest since May 2023. For homeowners with adjustable-rate mortgages, monthly payments would increase by an average of $200 to $300, adding $2,400 to $3,600 in annual repayment costs. Some households with volatile incomes could face a risk of falling behind. For prospective buyers, higher rates directly raised the cost of homeownership. Official data showed pending home sales fell 7.2% month over month in August, as many buyers chose to delay entering the market. People with fixed-rate mortgages or those buying homes entirely with cash were not directly affected by this rate adjustment.

The second group is ordinary consumers and borrowers. In a high-rate environment, rates on credit cards, auto loans, student loans, and other short-term credit also rise. Fed data showed the average U.S. credit-card annual percentage rate had reached 21.5%, while the average rate on new-car loans had risen to 7.2%. For people who rely on credit to maintain spending, monthly repayment pressure increased noticeably. Consumer confidence had declined for three consecutive months. Reports said U.S. retail sales fell 0.4% month over month in August, suggesting that the effect of high rates on consumption was already becoming visible.

The third group is workers and jobseekers. Reports from nonprofit organizations said that although the U.S. labor market remained resilient and unemployment stood at a low 3.8%, higher borrowing costs were raising companies' financing expenses. Hiring demand had begun to cool in rate-sensitive sectors such as technology, real estate, and manufacturing. Data showed that technology-sector layoffs reached 12,000 in August, up 15% from the previous month. Many companies had frozen hiring for recent graduates, making the job search more difficult for the class of 2026. Hiring in less rate-sensitive fields such as healthcare, education, and public utilities remained relatively stable.

The fourth group is investors. Financial analysts said the Nasdaq had declined 4.2% over the month following the rate increase, putting pressure on valuations for growth stocks, including AI companies. Unlike during the dot-com bubble in 2000, however, earnings expectations for the current AI sector remained relatively solid. The pullback was attributed mainly to valuation pressure from higher rates rather than deteriorating fundamentals. At the same time, higher Treasury yields made fixed-income assets more attractive. The average yield on U.S. Treasury funds rose to 4.5% in August, attracting safe-haven inflows, while the bond market's size grew 2.3% from the previous month.

## Responses and Upcoming Indicators

People with floating-rate debt should review their debt structure and repayment capacity. If they expect their income to remain stable, they could consider converting some floating-rate debt into fixed-rate obligations to lock in repayment costs and limit exposure to further increases. Prospective homebuyers were advised to consider delaying purchases and monitoring the Fed's policy signals. If inflation falls clearly and the Fed signals future cuts, they can reassess buying rather than taking on high carrying costs in the current environment.

Jobseekers, especially members of the class of 2026, were advised to prioritize openings in less rate-sensitive sectors such as healthcare and public utilities while building digital and technical skills to prepare for a possible cooling in the labor market. Businesses should manage cash flow carefully and control financing costs to reduce the risk of liquidity problems under high rates.

Investors were advised to maintain balanced portfolios and avoid excessive concentration in high-valuation growth stocks. They could consider increasing allocations to Treasury securities and high-dividend blue-chip stocks to reduce portfolio volatility. They also needed to watch the September CPI and nonfarm payrolls reports due in October. If inflation fell more than expected, the Fed might adjust its policy path, potentially causing asset-price volatility. Investors should prepare for that possibility.

title_en: Two Years After Hurricane Helene, Recovery Remains Incomplete and Some Residents Still Live in Risk Areas
body_en_md:
Two years after Hurricane Helene struck the southeastern United States, recovery work was still underway, and residents in some affected communities were still being allowed to live in areas exposed to flooding and landslides. Five people remained missing in western North Carolina. A study of the storm's effects was underway on the Clinch River in southwestern Virginia. North Carolina Gov. Stein attended a memorial event, while the city of Asheville encouraged fall visitors to travel to western North Carolina. Meanwhile, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) and National Weather Service (NWS) continued monitoring the Atlantic hurricane season, whose storm activity this year showed the influence of El Niño.

## Recovery Status

Hurricane Helene struck the southeastern United States in September 2024, causing severe flooding and landslides in western North Carolina, southwestern Virginia, and eastern Tennessee. In September 2026, two years later, several affected communities were still in the recovery process.

In western North Carolina, FOX Carolina News reported that five people remained missing. WCNC reported that reconstruction work was continuing in the Riverside Drive community. ABC11 News reported that Asheville was encouraging fall visitors to travel to western North Carolina as part of the recovery effort. North Carolina Gov. Stein attended an event marking the second anniversary of Hurricane Helene.

In southwestern Virginia, Cardinal News reported that a study was underway to assess Hurricane Helene's impact on the Clinch River. The research aims to understand the storm's long-term effects on the river system.

In South Carolina, WJBF reported that the Saluda County fire department was commemorating two firefighters who died during the storm. ABC7 WWSB also covered the second anniversary of Hurricane Helene.

In eastern Tennessee, knoxnews.com published a retrospective on the storm's second anniversary, including photographs and video.

## Missing People and Fatalities

According to FOX Carolina News, five people remained missing in western North Carolina, one of the continuing effects of Hurricane Helene. Their families were still waiting for information.

In Saluda County, South Carolina, WJBF reported that the local fire department was commemorating two firefighters who died during Hurricane Helene. Their families and colleagues held memorial activities on the second anniversary of the storm.

## Environmental Impact Study

Hurricane Helene had long-term environmental effects on affected areas. Cardinal News reported that a study was underway on the Clinch River in southwestern Virginia to assess the storm's impact on the river system. The research is expected to help explain the storm's long-term effects on the river ecosystem and provide scientific information for future recovery work.

## Atlantic Hurricane Season Context

This year's Atlantic hurricane season showed the influence of El Niño. The New York Times reported on storm activity on both U.S. coasts, noting that El Niño's effects were becoming apparent. U.S. News & World Report also covered this year's hurricane season.

According to NOAA, the Atlantic hurricane season runs from June 1 through November 30, with peak activity generally occurring from August through October. NOAA's National Hurricane Center monitors tropical systems throughout their life cycles and works with local National Weather Service forecast offices to issue advisories, watches, and warnings.

From 1990 through 2017, the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast regions received about 6% of tropical storms and hurricanes affecting the continental United States each year. In regional records, September was the most active month, followed by August. From 2000 through 2030, the number of hurricanes affecting the region was nearly twice the number during the previous two decades, 1980–2000.

## Historical Hurricane Data

According to NOAA historical data, records of Atlantic hurricane seasons date back to 1851. That was the first season included in the HURDAT database. Historically, 1886 was the most active hurricane season for the continental United States, with seven hurricanes making landfall. The database recorded the greatest number of major hurricanes in 1950, when eight major hurricanes occurred.

Research has found that the global proportion of Category 4 and 5 hurricanes has increased in recent decades amid climate change. From 1990 through 2021, the proportion of intense hurricanes increased as higher ocean-surface temperatures contributed to rapid intensification. Compared with 1980–1999, Category 4 and 5 hurricanes increased by 25% during 2000–2020.

Notable historical storms include the 1900 Galveston hurricane, which was only Category 4 but killed 8,000 people because no one expected it; the 1938 Long Island Express, the deadliest modern hurricane in the Northeast; Hurricane Andrew in 1992, which changed building codes; Hurricane Katrina in 2005, which caused $170 billion in damage; Hurricane Sandy in 2012, which exposed urban flood vulnerabilities; Hurricane Maria in 2017, which caused $92 billion in damage; and Hurricane Ida in 2021, cited as an example of climate change intensifying storms.

## Other Related Reports

Beyond coverage of Hurricane Helene, other related stories included a FOX Weather article in which Steve Bender reflected on the storm's second anniversary. Gulf Coast News and Weather reported on the fourth anniversary of Hurricane Ian and differences between this year's hurricane season and last year's. WINK News reported that the Orange Harbor community was celebrating its recovery four years after Hurricane Ian destroyed 80 homes. Bay News 9 reported that a memorial bench swept away during Hurricane Helene two years earlier had been found in Bermuda.

ABC7 San Francisco also reported that Hurricane Polo drenched the Mexican coast and that Nolo was approaching Hawaii.

## What to Watch Next

Residents and visitors in areas affected by Hurricane Helene should pay attention to several issues:

1. **Reconstruction:** The Riverside Drive community in western North Carolina and other affected communities were still rebuilding. Residents should learn about progress and future plans for their own neighborhoods.

2. **Missing people:** Five people remained missing in western North Carolina. Families and others following the case can monitor updates from local law-enforcement agencies.

3. **Environmental research:** The Clinch River study in southwestern Virginia is examining Hurricane Helene's effects. Its findings may help explain the storm's long-term impact on the river system and inform future recovery work.

4. **Hurricane season:** The Atlantic hurricane season runs from June 1 through November 30, with peak activity from August through October. NOAA's NHC and the NWS continue to monitor storms. Residents and visitors should follow forecasts and warnings.

5. **Visitors:** Asheville has encouraged fall visitors to travel to western North Carolina. Visitors should learn about local recovery conditions, respect affected communities, and take safety precautions.

6. **Climate change:** Research indicates that the global share of Category 4 and 5 hurricanes has increased amid climate change. Residents and policymakers should monitor this trend and prepare accordingly.

Residents affected by Hurricane Helene should follow updates from local governments and relief organizations, learn about reconstruction progress and future plans, and avoid areas that remain hazardous. Visitors should check local conditions before traveling, respect affected communities, and take appropriate precautions.

Overall, two years after Hurricane Helene, recovery was still underway, and some communities continued to allow residents to live in areas exposed to risk. The missing-person cases remained unresolved, environmental research was continuing, and this year's Atlantic hurricane activity showed the influence of El Niño. Residents and visitors should continue to monitor forecasts and warnings.
